# Billing: usage and spend on Datum Cloud

This describes how Datum Cloud meters usage and prices it, and how to read
the billing tools' results. The tools read one project's usage, as the person
asking, in the project the conversation is about.

## Usage

Every service reports what a project consumes on meters. A meter has:

- A name, e.g. "ALB Requests", and a meter name naming the service that owns
  it, e.g. networking.datumapis.com/gateway/requests.
- A unit. Byte meters are shown in KB, MB and GB of 1024, the same GB byte
  meters are priced in. Byte-seconds (memory held over time) are shown as
  GB-hours (GB·h), millicore-seconds as vCPU time (vCPU·h), allocated CPU as
  vCPU, durations as s, m, h and d, and everything else (requests, tokens,
  queries) as a plain count.
- An aggregation. Most meters sum (Sum, Count): the period's value is the
  total consumed. Some are gauges: Latest is the most recent reading (e.g.
  allocated CPU, active DNS records) and Max the peak. A gauge's value is a
  level, not an amount used, and the tools mark it "latest" or "peak". Never
  add gauge readings across days.
- Dimensions it can be broken down by, e.g. region, model, httproute_name
  (an ALB) or project_name. list_meters shows each meter's dimensions.

A meter with no usage in a period is left out of results, and the result says
how many were left out (metersWithoutUsage). A deprecated meter only appears
while it still has usage.

## Spend

Spend is what the usage costs, priced the way the invoice prices it: with the
prices of the billing account's plan in effect at the time, with tiered prices
continuing from usage earlier in the billing period. It is before taxes,
credits and discounts, so the invoice total can differ.

- Spend is per meter and for the whole period. A breakdown or daily view
  shows usage only.
- A meter without spend has no price on the plan; it doesn't mean it is free
  of charge elsewhere on the invoice.
- spendUnavailable means the price could not be worked out for that meter or
  the total. Say so rather than guessing a figure.
- A project's spend is priced as if its usage were the billing account's only
  usage, so for tiered prices the project's share of an organization's bill
  can differ.

## Billing cycles

Usage is reported for billing cycles, which come from the billing account's
payment terms: an invoice day of the month and a frequency (monthly,
quarterly or annual). The current cycle runs from its start to now; the
previous cycle is the one before it. When the billing account can't be read,
cycles are assumed to be calendar months and the result's notes say so. Any
other range can be read with from and to.

## Billing accounts, payment methods and invoices

A project is billed to one billing account, which belongs to its
organization. Several projects can share an account.

- An account's phase is Provisioning (being set up), Ready (can be billed),
  Suspended or Archived. When it isn't Ready, its status and issues say why,
  often a default payment method that isn't active.
- The account's payment terms set its billing cycle (invoice day and
  frequency) and how many days an invoice has to be paid (net days). Some
  accounts pay by invoice under an arrangement with its own net days and
  credit limit instead of by card.
- The plan is the Offer whose prices the account's usage is charged at.
- Payment methods are cards or US bank accounts. Only enough to recognise
  one is shown: brand or bank, last four digits, and a card's expiry. A
  payment method is Pending or AwaitingConfirmation while it is being set up,
  Active once confirmed, and Failed with a reason when it can't be used. The
  default payment method is the one the account is charged to.

Invoices are issued for each billing cycle once it closes. An invoice only
appears once it has been issued, so the current cycle's charges show as spend
(usage_summary), not as an invoice.

- Open: issued, payment outstanding (including while a payment is
  processing). PastDue: not paid by its due date. Paid. Void: cancelled, or
  written off as uncollectible.
- Total is what the invoice charges; amount due is what is left to pay.
- The link opens the invoice's hosted page, where it can be viewed,
  downloaded and paid. It is kept current, so it always opens.
- A problem on an invoice, such as a currency that doesn't match the
  account's, is reported with it.

The assistant can't change any of this. Payment methods, the default payment
method and invoices are managed on the organization's Billing page in the
Datum Cloud portal, by someone with an organization role that can edit
billing.

## Which tool to use

- usage_summary: what did this project use and what does it cost, for the
  current or previous billing cycle or a date range. Start here.
- usage_breakdown: what is driving a meter's usage, split by one dimension
  (e.g. region, model, ALB). Optionally one meter.
- usage_daily: when did usage change, per day. Optionally one meter.
- list_meters: what each meter measures, its unit, aggregation and
  dimensions.
- get_billing_account: the project's billing account: status and why,
  currency, plan, payment terms, current cycle and default payment method.
- list_payment_methods: the account's payment methods and their status.
- list_invoices: the account's invoices, newest first, with status, amounts,
  due dates and links.

## Scope and access

The usage tools read only this project's usage, which needs the billing
viewer role that an organization's Viewer, Editor and Owner roles include.
The billing account, payment methods and invoices belong to the
organization, so reading them needs an organization role even when the
project's usage is readable.
Organization-wide usage, across every project, is on the organization's Usage
page in the Datum Cloud portal, or `datumctl billing usage --org <org>`.
